genericProblem: A declared UI surface can be contradicted by its own wireframe when it renders sibling shell controls, adjacent pages, or suppressed implementation annotations as though they belonged to that surface.
rootCauseClass: surface declaration and visual denominator were reviewed separately rather than as an exact per-screen ownership set; the same pass also failed to verify that every input-bearing surface carried its control-dependency denominator.
searchedSurfaces: all IA01/IA02 Screen declarations, USER_VISIBLE_COPY fields and ASCII wireframes
all IA01/IA02 input-bearing surfaces and existing form-control dependency tables
the reusable UI interaction template and P6 final-design standard
searchQueries: 可使用的功能菜单|当前集团空间.*编码|不显示|\[用户 v\]|可查看范围：机构名称
counterexamples: A content page may name its route-level shell in HOST_AND_ENTRY, but its own wireframe cannot draw a sibling Header control as page content.
A Header control may explain that an owner result refreshes menus, but it cannot render the menu, user avatar, or a separate Header control as part of that one-control wireframe.
An input with no upstream control is not exempt from a dependency row; the row must explicitly state no dependency and owner revalidation.

A data-scope selector that is declared as a Header control or Drawer contradicts a verified legacy visual baseline when both v1 and v4 place the entry at the operations shell's side-menu footer; that mismatch must be resolved as a physical-surface correction, without inheriting legacy local authorization state.

findings.evidence: IA02-OPERATIONS-SHELL-HEADER declared one Header control while its initial wireframe also rendered menu, user-avatar and data-scope siblings; IA02-PLATFORM-WORKSPACE-CONTEXT declared a content empty state while drawing the separate workspace Header control.

The global scan found only two dependency-table anchors although multiple IA01/IA02 input-bearing surfaces were already declared; the template rule was not retroactively audited as an exact screen denominator.

IA01-USER-INVITATION-ACTIONS simultaneously drew an inline create form and row-level resend/cancel while separately declaring a create Drawer, detail Drawer and action Modal for the same tasks; the frozen list-detail-action standard requires the business action to originate from detail, not a list action column.

Dexter's accepted Drawer requirement is a searchable appointment-organization choice followed by same-type roles. Current WorkspaceUserService.candidatesForOperations returns only the server-resolved task scope, so it proves owner revalidation but not the required multi-candidate selection. The IA must retain Dexter's required user task and surface the final P6 contract/owner closure rather than falsely claim current bytes already support it.

IA02 initially declared the range entry in the Header and its selection surface as a Drawer. The reopened v1 OperationsShell/DataNodeSwitcherPort and v4 OperationsGlobalWorkScope both place the entry in menuFooterRender; v4 opens a right-bottom Popover, while v1 proves upstream selection clears downstream levels. IA02 now uses a side-footer summary control plus Popover, owner-entry-only cascade, and no inherited local scope authority.
